title: Ordinary inverse-image and balanced scalar-tower square
statement:
Let $h:\operatorname{Sh}(C_X)\to\operatorname{Sh}(C_Y)$ be a morphism of topoi, on sites small in the module universe [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism, def-weil-size-convention], and let $A_Y\xrightarrow{a}B_Y\xrightarrow{b}C_Y$ be commutative ring sheaves. On $X$ take their inverse images and maps. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and sheafified balanced tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. For $r\to s$ put $E_{rs}^V=s_V\otimes_{r_V}-$, with its first-factor action, and let $h_r^*$ mean inverse image of $r_Y$-modules. Let
$$\chi_h^{rs}:h_s^*E_{rs}^Y\xrightarrow{\sim}E_{rs}^Xh_r^*$$
be the comparison of the balanced coequalizers: inverse image of the scalar and module action arrows is identified with the corresponding pair over $X$. Let
$$t_V:E_{BC}^VE_{AB}^V\xrightarrow{\sim}E_{AC}^V,\qquad c\otimes(b'\otimes m)\mapsto c\,b(b')\otimes m$$
be scalar reassociation, inverse to $c\otimes m\mapsto c\otimes(1\otimes m)$. Then the following equality holds as natural transformations of $C_X$-module sheaves:
$$\chi_h^{AC}\circ h_C^*(t_Y)=(t_Xh_A^*)\circ E_{BC}^X(\chi_h^{AB})\circ(\chi_h^{BC}E_{AB}^Y).$$
The equality also holds termwise on cochain complexes [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. This statement concerns the specified balanced quotient maps, with their coefficient actions, and asserts no derived-functor existence or K-flat preservation.

proof.text:
Write $F=h^{-1}$ on underlying sheaves of sets, and transport ring and module operations by its finite-product comparison [def-weil-pbc-algebraic-inverse-image]. Let $p_{rs}^V:s_V\times M\to E_{rs}^VM$ be the sheafified pure pairing and $u_{rs}^V(m)=p_{rs}^V(1,m)$. The normalized inverse-image tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-inverse-image-tensor-comparison], applied to the $r_Y$-modules $s_Y,M$, gives
$$\chi_{h,M}^{rs}F(p_{rs}^Y)=p_{rs}^X$$
after the canonical identification $F(s_Y\times M)=s_X\times F(M)$. This is the specified balanced-coequalizer comparison: its defining factorization has precisely this equation, which determines the tensor map [def-weil-pbc-ringed-tensor-section-calculus]. The equation is an equality of maps of sheaves, so it applies to arbitrary generalized sections over every test sheaf on $X$. The comparison is $s_X$-linear: multiplication by $z$ on the first input sends either side on $(s,m)$ to $p_{rs}^X(zs,m)$; transport preserves ring multiplication and the module action. Tensor universality gives the action equation on the quotient. In particular $\chi^{rs}F(u_{rs}^Y)=u_{rs}^X$ since $F$ transports the unit section.

proof.text: For $V=X,Y$, the displayed formula for $t_V$ respects both balances. The $B_V$ relation gives the same value $c\,b_V(\beta)b_V(b')\otimes m$ from $c\,b_V(\beta)\otimes(b'\otimes m)$ and $c\otimes(\beta b'\otimes m)$. The inner $A_V$ relation gives $c\,b_V(b')b_Va_V(\alpha)\otimes m=c\,b_V(b')\otimes\alpha m$. Additivity in each input is distributivity. The inverse insertion respects the $A_V$ relation since $1\otimes\alpha m=a_V(\alpha)\otimes m$ and the outer $B_V$ balance moves $a_V(\alpha)$ to $c$. Thus these formulas descend through the balanced tensors and sheafification [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-weil-pbc-ringed-tensor-section-calculus]. Their composites are identities: one gives $c\otimes m$, and the other gives $c\,b_V(b')\otimes(1\otimes m)=c\otimes(b'\otimes m)$. The maps are $C_V$-linear because their first factor is multiplied by $c$. In particular, putting $w_Y=u_{BC}^Y\circ u_{AB}^Y$ on underlying sheaves, $t_Yw_Y=u_{AC}^Y$. These verifications use no flatness or invertibility.

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product), its bilinear universal property; Tag 03EL (lemma-tensor-product-pullback), normalized comparison; blueprint det-prop-scalar-six-pullback.proof.md (3)

proof.text: Fix $M$ and put $D=C_Y\otimes_{B_Y}(B_Y\otimes_{A_Y}M)$ and $P=C_X\otimes_{A_X}F(M)$. For $C_X$-linear $d,e:F(D)\to P$, equality follows from $dF(w_Y)=eF(w_Y)$. Indeed, the underlying sheaf adjunction [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism] gives adjuncts $\bar d=h_*d\circ\eta_D$ and $\bar e=h_*e\circ\eta_D$. They are $C_Y$-linear: naturality of $\eta$ for addition and scalar action, with the product comparison, gives $\eta_D(cz)=\eta_C(c)\eta_D(z)$, and $h_*d,h_*e$ respect the transported action [def-weil-pbc-algebraic-inverse-image]. Twice applying the extension/restriction adjunction of [def-weil-pbc-ringed-tensor-section-calculus] shows a $C_Y$-linear map from $D$ is determined by its composite with $w_Y$: the two adjunction units insert $1\otimes-$ in succession. Naturality of $\eta$ now gives $\bar d w_Y=h_*(dF(w_Y))\eta_M$ and the analogous equation for $e$. Hence the assumed equality implies $\bar d=\bar e$, and injectivity of the underlying adjunction implies $d=e$. This is a direct composite of the cited Hom bijections; it does not assume points of the topos or sectionwise surjectivity of a tensor pairing.

proof.text:
Take $d=\chi_h^{AC}F(t_Y)$ and $e=t_X\,E_{BC}^X(\chi_h^{AB})\,\chi_h^{BC}$, with the indicated whiskering at $M$. Both are $C_X$-linear by steps 1 and 2. On $F(w_Y)$, the first route is
$$F(M)\xrightarrow{F(u_{AC}^Y)}F(C_Y\otimes_{A_Y}M)\xrightarrow{\chi^{AC}}C_X\otimes_{A_X}F(M),$$
so its value is $1\otimes m$. For the second route, step 1 for $B\to C$ sends the transported outer unit to $1\otimes F(u_{AB}^Y)(m)$. Extension of scalars of $\chi^{AB}$ sends this to $1\otimes\chi^{AB}F(u_{AB}^Y)(m)=1\otimes(1\otimes m)$. Finally $t_X$ sends it to $1\otimes m$. These are equalities of sheaf maps from $F(M)$, using the unit-normalized comparison in step 1. More generally, on the transported generalized triple $(c,b',m)$ the first route is $c\,b_X(b')\otimes m$, while the second is $c\otimes(b'\otimes m)\mapsto c\,b_X(b')\otimes m$; $F$ transports multiplication and $b_Y$ to multiplication and $b_X$. Thus the computation uses the actual final-ring action, rather than an unspecified isomorphism. Step 3 proves the required equality on all of $F(D)$.

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product), its bilinear universal property; Tag 03EL (lemma-tensor-product-pullback), normalized comparison; blueprint det-prop-scalar-six-pullback.proof.md (3)

proof.text: The equality holds for every $A_Y$-module $M$. The comparisons in step 1 are natural; the balancing formulas in step 2 are natural because a module map $v:M\to N$ changes $c\,b_V(b')\otimes m$ to $c\,b_V(b')\otimes v(m)$ along either route [def-weil-pbc-ringed-tensor-section-calculus]. Therefore the component equality is the displayed equality of natural transformations. For a cochain complex $M^\bullet$, apply this equality in each degree. Naturality with respect to each differential $d^n$ says that both component families commute with the differentials, so they are equal maps of complexes by the definition [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. There is no totalization or exchange of tensor factors, and hence no sign to choose. This proves exactly the termwise assertion, without localization or a K-flat hypothesis.
